Meanwhile, tokenization went sovereign in India and Washington's turf war over crypto markets escalated. 🔥 Hot CPI Sets Up a Fed Rate Hike and Whipsaws Bitcoin Core CPI rose a faster-than-forecast 0.3% in August, even as the annual pace held at 2.4% — the slowest since early 2021. Rate-hike odds for the September FOMC jumped toward 70%, knocking Bitcoin below $77,000 before buyers absorbed the dip and lifted it back toward $80,000, with long-end bond yields printing a 22-year high. Read full story 📉 Bitcoin ETFs Bleed $449M in Three Days Spot Bitcoin funds logged their largest single-day outflow since July, with roughly $449 million pulled across three consecutive sessions. Ether products moved the other way, attracting fresh money — a sharp divergence in institutional appetite heading into the Fed meeting. More details 🛡️ Blockstream Rejects Ransom as Liquid Attackers Hold ~600 BTC Blockstream refused to pay a ransom after the Liquid Network breach, with close to 600 BTC still under attacker control. Transactions have resumed on the sidechain while peg-outs stay disabled, and the company has signalled it will not negotiate with the group. Read more ⚖️ Revised CLARITY Act Puts "Non-Decentralized" DeFi in Scope Republicans circulated fresh bill text that narrows exemptions for DeFi operators and front-ends retaining meaningful control, alongside tweaks to credit union provisions. The legislation still needs 60 votes when the Senate returns from recess, and its path remains far from settled. See details 🇮🇳 India Starts Tokenizing Its $620B Corporate Bond Market SEBI's Demat 2.0 pilot converts corporate bonds into digital tokens with payment settled through the RBI's wholesale digital rupee. Secondary trading and retail access are planned for later phases, making it one of the largest sovereign-scale tokenization pushes announced so far.
